findings.title: pull_request_target checks out untrusted PR code
findings.description: A workflow triggered by 'pull_request_target' (which runs with repo secrets and a write token) also checks out the pull request's head. Attacker-controlled code then runs with access to secrets.
findings.impact: A malicious PR can exfiltrate all repository secrets and push to the repo (full supply-chain compromise).
findings.remediation: Use 'pull_request' for untrusted code, or check out the base ref only and never build/run PR code in a privileged context.
findings.poc:
# Patch: split trusted/untrusted work
on: pull_request        # not pull_request_target
permissions:
  contents: read
# If you must use pull_request_target, do NOT checkout PR head
# and never run its scripts with secrets present.

findings.title: Script injection via untrusted github.event data
findings.description: Untrusted event data is interpolated directly into a shell command; an attacker controls that value.
findings.impact: Arbitrary command execution on the runner with access to the job's secrets and token.
findings.remediation: Never inline ${{ github.event.* }} into run steps. Pass it through an environment variable and reference it quoted.
findings.poc:
# Patch: bind to env, then use the quoted variable
  - env:
      TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
    run: echo "$TITLE"

findings.title: Third-party action not pinned to a commit SHA: some/action@main
findings.description: The action is referenced by a mutable tag/branch. If that tag is moved (or the action is compromised), malicious code runs in your pipeline.
findings.impact: Supply-chain compromise: the action author (or an attacker who hijacks the tag) can run code with your secrets.
findings.remediation: Pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA and review updates via Dependabot.
findings.poc:
# Patch: pin to an immutable SHA
  uses: some/action@<full-40-char-commit-sha>  # was @main

findings.title: Secret printed to build logs
findings.description: A step echoes a secret; build logs are often broadly readable and archived.
findings.impact: The secret is exposed to anyone who can read pipeline logs.
findings.remediation: Never print secrets. Use masked env vars and remove debug echoes.

findings.title: Workflow token granted write-all permissions
findings.description: The GITHUB_TOKEN is granted broad write permissions; any compromised step can abuse them.
findings.impact: A compromised step can push code, publish packages, or alter the repo.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege: default to 'contents: read' and grant only the specific scopes a job needs.
findings.poc:
# Patch: least-privilege token
permissions:
  contents: read

findings.title: Remote script piped straight into a shell
findings.description: A pipeline step downloads a script and executes it immediately; the remote content is unverified and can change at any time.
findings.impact: If the remote host or content is tampered with, arbitrary code runs in the pipeline.
findings.remediation: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum/signature, then execute.
findings.poc:
# Patch: verify before executing
curl -fsSL https://host/install.sh -o install.sh
echo '<sha256>  install.sh' | sha256sum -c -
bash install.sh
